text:
ana: heads-up — past 6 hours we saw a ~28% jump in GPU-hours billed while tokens/sec is flat. cost run is spiky, curious if it's real or instrumentation noise

mike: seen it too, p50 latency up ~20ms across EU region around 05:00-07:30 UTC, but tokens/sec unchanged. possible batching or small-request noise? :thinking:

jules: could be prefix cache churn + sudden model-mix shift. we rolled the assistant-lite model at 04:50 for canary, maybe traffic hitting a non-quantized variant?

ana: infra-bot reported autoscale events: `scale_up pool-gpu-eu-2 from 18->26 at 05:12` then `scale_down to 20 at 06:05` — I pasted the bot logs below:
```
infra-bot: [05:12:08] autoscaler: pool-gpu-eu-2 scale_up reason=cpu_pressure target=26
infra-bot: [05:13:02] route-checker: rerouting 12% requests to fallback-model-lr
infra-bot: [06:05:47] autoscaler: pool-gpu-eu-2 scale_down target=20 reason=latency_recovery
```

mike: interesting — reroute to fallback-model-lr could cause more GPU cycles if fallback is less optimized. any change in avg sequence length?

jules: quick check: avg_seq_len by model for the window 04:30-07:30 UTC:
```
assistant-main:  68 -> 70 (stable)
assistant-lite: 28 -> 85 (canary traffic seems to include long prompts)
fallback-model-lr: 120 -> 130 (higher KV usage)
```

ana: that explains extra KV cache misses and compute per request. assistant-lite canary seems to have a bug concatenating system prompts, inflating sequence length. cc @mike can we throttle canary and revert?
mike: yes, pausing canary now. running revert: `deployctl rollback assistant-lite canary-2026-03-18`

sre-rover: also noticed increased network retransmits from EU AZ-b1 at 05:05-05:30 — packet loss could cause timeouts and retries K/V reloads. infra-router logs attached (snippet):
```
[snippet] 05:07:12 conn=1439 status=RST reason=peer_unreachable
[snippet] 05:09:03 conn=1490 retransmit=6 rtt=310ms
```

jules: so signal decomposition: 1) canary bug -> longer seqs -> more GPU cycles 2) fallback routing -> heavier models used 3) transient network loss -> retries + KV misses -> extra compute. all additive.

ana: can we quantify headroom impact? i want to know how many GPU-hours attributable to each factor to inform chargebacks. mike, can you run the throughput model with these adjustments? inputs: baseline QPS, seq_len_dist, cache_hit_rate change from 0.72 -> 0.49, model mix shift 8%->22% fallback, retry overhead +12% compute. output: GPU-hours delta per factor and confidence intervals.
mike: on it. I'll run the simulator with synthetic traces and get back in ~30m. quick command I used:
```
python tools/simulate_capacity.py --trace bigquery:projects/redwood/datasets/infra_traces:2026_03_18 --start 04:30 --end 07:30 --params '{"cache_hit_rate":0.49,"seq_len_multipliers":{"assistant-lite":3.0,"fallback-model-lr":1.6}}' --output /tmp/191234-sim.json
```

ana: also include cost model (on-demand vs reserved delta), and show percent of extra GPU-hours falling on Dedicated vs Hosted pools. need that for finance.

infra-bot: [06:05] simulation-job-queue: job 7d9f queued by mike; est runtime 18m

mike: sim done earlier than expected. top-line: +26% GPU-hours for the window. breakdown by factor:
- canary seq inflation: +12% GPU-hours (+0.45 GPU-hours per 1k req)
- fallback model mix: +7%
- network retries & KV churn: +5%
- autoscaler thrash (spin-up inefficiency): +2%
confidence: medium (sampling noise ~3-4%)

jules: run-level suggestion: set canary throttling to 2% traffic and add seq-length alert for assistant-lite. Also increase cache TTL in EU for 1 hour to reduce cold misses while we fix prompt concatenation.

ana: ops action items:
- revert assistant-lite canary (mike) — in progress
- add seq_len anomaly alert (jules)
- temporary EU cache TTL bump + purge old keys (infra team) — @infra-bot create task
- finance: compute chargeback breakdown (ana)

mike: started rollback at 06:15, finished 06:19. rolling eviction of inflated KV entries scheduled at 06:30.

infra-bot: [06:32] task created: EU-cache-ttl-bump by jules due 2026-03-19

sre-rover: follow-up: let's also add a synthetic load test for long-tail prompt sequences in staging to catch sequence-length regressions before canary. I can script that.

ana: agreed. once we have the GPU-hour attribution numbers I'll post a short note to finance and product about the cost hit and recommended changes to canary gating. thanks team :heart:

mike: posting sim artifacts here: https://internal.redwood/sims/1912345678/results.json (contains per-model GPU-hour deltas and per-AZ network correlation)

jules: added alert rule PR: `infra/alerts/seq_len_anomaly.yml` — one-liner rule, sensitivity tuned for 99th pct change.

ana: closing thread after finance ack. good triage, this was a clean deconvolution. :tada:
